Drakensberg Boys Choir turns 50..The Hills are Alive

By: Diana Lucas | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We celebrate one of South Africa's own, the Drakensberg Boys Choir turns 50

Summary:
The Drakensberg Boys Choir turns 50, and we celebrate this truly South African icon. We look back at some of the renowned musicians who have passed through their doors. Look at some of the student their today and find out why they are inspired by this very different school and we take a look at the history of the school and choir.
To highlight our story we we will be there at their concert they will be giving to celebrate 50 and still going strong…the hills will be truly alive

Press Release:


Drakensberg Boys Choir: celebrating 50 years
In 1967, 21 pupils from around South Africa were selected to sing in what would one day become the internationally renowned, Drakensberg Boys Choir.
Over the past 50 years, some of the country’s most celebrated, classically-trained musicians have passed through the school’s doors, using choral music as a
vehicle for holistic education. Carte Blanche celebrates the angelic voices of this world-famous choir

Script:


Link
For the last 50 years its voices like that angelic majestic that have dominated this valley here in the Drakensberg Mountains,

V/O 10
This is Drakensberg Boys Choir School, Nathan Julius is one of it’s graduates .. the next stop in his musical career path is a renowned music university in Switzerland.

Nathan Julius
Class of 2013

Nathan: I’m going to Switzerland in Basel to study early music.
Bongani: How big an achievement is that.
Nathan: It’s quiet an achievement actually they told me they saw something special in my voice so that’s quiet nice being a Drakie set you up for good things in life.

V/O 10 sec
120 boys between 9 to 15 years old attend Drakensberg Boys. Executive Head Andrew Stead believes central to their ethos is the boy’s own commitment.

Andrew Stead
Executive Head: Drakensberg Boys Choir

Andrew: My first question to a boy is do you want to be here…it’s the boy that wants to be here and he must be passionate about music.
Bongani: In 2017 could a critic say this is an elitist enclave in the mountains?
Andrew: The truth is very different we have a fantastically diverse group of young men and about 30 to 33% of those are sponsored by corporates. My personal belief is that every boy should be sponsored because we are quiet a unique South African brand.

Sihle Manonyane
Prefect
 
Sihle
I have a passion for music so we came here for a choir trip and I was really impressed with the performance and vibe of the school,

Bongani: So what was it like for you to come here and learn all this old stuff that Liam had already learnt.
Sihle: It was pretty tough I also had no musical exp just knew how to sing so I just put my heard down and worked hard
Bongani: my first thought when I came here this is right in the middle of the mountains this is a bit like Hogwarts.
Sihle: I thought so too when I came here and was a new boy I told someone this is basically like Hogwarts we sing and it’s all based on the Dragons of the mountains.

Link
In 1967 this was just another farm in the Drakensberg but it took the vision and passion of a man who was devoted to music to turn it into a national treasure

V/O 7 sec
Founder, John Tangay, auditioned and enrolled 21 pupils, within a year 15 more boys had joined his little singing school.

Andrew: On the one hand the thought of someone opening a choir school in 1967 on the tip of Africa its like a crazy idea isn’t it and yet its been so successful

V/O 4 sec - 3
And last weekend the school celebrated 50 year’s with a weekend of music

Link
The tradition of the Boys Choir is a centuries old one when men and woman couldn’t perform sacred music together in public spaces here in the Drakensberg tradition meets modernity with drama passion and excitement.

V/O 3 sec
Topping the programme was Carmina Burana,

Bernard Kruger
Artistic Director: Drakensberg Boys Choir

This work that we are performing Carmena Burana is a work the DBC has performed many times in the last 50 years we keep coming back to it because it’s a phenomenal piece of work because it suits the choir so well full of rythmn it’s full of exciting moments everything that can appeal to boys who sing is in there.

V/O 11 sec
Bernard Kruger aka the Chef is the school’s Musical director…. with 1 600 boys auditioning for 35 places last year his nod to who gets selected is a very valuable one.

Bongani: When does this magic happen when do you hear a voice and say that’s the one?
Bernard: I would say within the first 5 seconds if a boy walks in I can already see if you are a Drakie or not its in your eyes and then once they start singing that’s something that we can even teach them but you cant teach some one to have that spark.

Kigen Chepkonga
New Boy 2017
 
I was in choir at my old school because I loved singing I loved music do I did audition during that I realised this school could take me places and it would really build me up.

Alec Gibson
New Boy 2017
 
Bongani: So when you were told you were in?
A: I knew this is where I belong because at my old school I was the odd one out because I was the choir boy and all my other friends were rugby mates and I just thought I cd fit more here because I am not the only one who can sing.

Bernard:: When they start here we call them new boys, the rehearsal process and teaching them the discipline of standing in a rehearsal and breathing together…boys are not used to that nb for me that they are boys /// I would hate for them to be robots must be flamboyant they have to be creative and still naughty .

V/O 6 / 7
Joining the concert are some old Drakies….like tenor Nicholas Nicolaides one of our most celebrated concert performers.

he was 10 years old when he started at the school in 1988.
 
Nicholas Nicolaidis.
Class of 1991

Nicholas: I arrived at a little school it was like a farm school, this was the Hall and where we had concerts this was we rehearsed?
Bongani: In this little space?
Nicholas: Yes in this little space, It was an Afrikaans school I was an English speaking boy they had never seen anyone quiet like me before somebody 4 f 3 with dwarfism and not only that my good friend Zwai Bale arrived to and he was the first black boy ever to be accepted at the school
Bongani: What was that changes a period of uncertainty school and nation like nestled in this little valley?
Nicholas: It was really fantastic because we went through the angst of 1994 before 1994.
because the community here had to deal with with what it was like for people of diff colour, different race different looks diff types of people what is it like to work together towards a common goal and we could do it through music, music was our vehicle vehicle of song and if you sing together you realise we are all the same because you all need to breathe in time and we all need to deliver in time so we all need to resonate together.

V/O 11 sec
It was the international tours that really made the Drakensberg Boys Choir world renowned and a South African brand…for 49 years they have taken to the international stage at least once a year.

Liam Muller
Head Boy

Whenever you go on international tour you get one of these…Namibia…Holland japan
L I guess its every concert story when were singing afterwards we come outside and that’s when all the cameras come out and then all the flashes are coming out and you just have to keep on smiling.

Nicholas
What did the school do for you?
It laid the ground work fro my musical development because I realised when I was here that I was being invested in…staff boys community investing in like MGs 10 000 hours that when I left I was already on my path
You had found your voice
You are right I realised I cd do this for the rest of my life because when we sing together it’s the Ubuntu…. once you share the stage with them you are connected.
